title: linux: diagnose swap thrashing that makes a host unresponsive
scenario: On linux, an expert-level problem demanding deep causal reasoning: Un host e' quasi irresponsivo per swap thrashing: la memoria e' sovraccarica e il paging domina. Stabilizza senza uccidere ciecamente processi critici. Multiple plausible causes; only evidence separates them.

environment.task: diagnose swap thrashing that makes a host unresponsive

initial_state: # fixture: linux host prepared for 'diagnose swap thrashing that makes a host unresponsive'
expected_reasoning: Thrashing = working set exceeds RAM, so paging dominates — relieve pressure, don't just kill at random.
Identify the memory hog and whether swap is undersized or a leak drives it.
Relieve pressure (bound the hog, add RAM/swap headroom) and set limits so one process can't thrash the host.

ground_truth.task: diagnose swap thrashing that makes a host unresponsive

possible_mistakes: kill -9 processes blindly under pressure, hitting a critical one.
Add huge swap, masking a leak with slow death.
hints: Thrashing shows as high major-fault rate + swap IO.
Bound the hog with a cgroup limit.
alternative_solution: Use a memory cgroup / earlyoom so the offender is capped before the host thrashes.
edge_cases: A memory-mapped file, not anonymous memory, drives the paging.
